Bt protein concentration varies with silk age and that pyramided hybrids significantly reduce feeding injury to the ear tip and kernels.
Bt proteins are highest in the silk, ear tip, and husk, and that the feeding injury and feeding behavior of H zea larvae are not affected by the presence of Bt proteins in corn ears.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential for H. zea to develop resistance to Bt corn hybrids.
the development, survival and feeding behavior of corn earworm larvae relative to Bt concentrations in different corn ear tissues.
the development, survival and feeding behavior of H. zea in relation to Bt protein concentration in corn ear tissues and how it can influence resistance management strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bt proteins are not evenly distributed within the ear and this could have implications for resistance management.
Bt hybrids with high Cry1F and Vip3A concentrations in the silk tissue and low Cry1F and high Cry2Ab2 concentrations in the tip tissue may provide the most durable protection against H. zea.
the Bt proteins Cry1F and Vip3A are effective in reducing H. zea feeding injury in the silk, ear tip, and kernels of corn.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pyramided Bt hybrid expressing Vip 3A incurred no feeding injury to the ear tip or kernel tissues and the feeding behavior of H.zea larvae did not differ between Bt and conventional hybrids.
H. zea is a generalist feeder that can feed on Bt and non Bt hybrids, but the Bt hybrids reduce feeding injury and survival.
H. zea is capable of surviving on all Bt hybrids tested and that Bt proteins are not a barrier to larval development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Bt corn hybrids expressing pyramided proteins are effective at protecting the silk, tip tissue, and kernels from feeding injury and larval development.
the spatial and temporal variation in Bt protein concentrations can influence the risk of resistance to transgenic Bt crops.
the concentrations of Bt proteins in corn ear tissues are heterogeneous, which can influence H. zea feeding injury and development.
